models_evaluated: six commonly used AI chatbots (not named in the abstract)

links.outcome: Red-flag recognition and potentially misleading/unsafe responses in simulated nipple discharge consultations
links.effect: Red-flag recognition 90.6% (1174/1296); 8/216 (3.7%) potentially misleading, none unsafe; 4 of 8 misleading responses were due to missed red-flag features.
links.quote: The overall red-flag recognition rate was 90.6 % (1174 of 1296; 95 % CI, 87.8 %-93.2 %), and the median response-level recognition rate was 100.0 % (interquartile range [IQR], 85.7 %-100.0 %).

links.outcome: Recognition of safety-critical red flags and escalation recommendations in chatbot responses
links.effect: Most red flags recognized (90.6%), but some responses had incomplete red-flag safety-netting; 3 of 8 misleading responses had poor actionability or insufficient action-oriented recommendations.
links.quote: Nevertheless, some responses demonstrated incomplete red-flag safety-netting and lacked specific recommendations for subsequent action.

unlisted_practices: Incorporating structured red-flag screening and explicit triage recommendations into patient-facing AI symptom chatbots

screen.reason: Evaluates the triage safety and red-flag recognition of six commercial LLM chatbots on simulated patient queries without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment intervention.
